segments.arabic:
١١٤٣٠- ضباعة بنت عامر
بن قرط بن سلمة بن قشير «٣» بن كعب بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صعصعة.
ذكرها أبو نعيم،
وأخرج من طريق عبد اللَّه بن الأجلح، عن الكلبيّ، أخبرني عبد الرحمن العامريّ، عن أشياخ من قومه، قالوا: أتانا رسول اللَّه ﷺ ونحن بعكاظ، فدعانا إلى نصرته ومنعته، فأجبناه إذ جاء بيحرة»
بن فهراس القشيريّ، فغمز شاكلة ناقة رسول اللَّه ﷺ فقمصت به، فألقته، وعندنا يومئذ ضباعة بنت عامر بن قرط، وكانت من النسوة اللاتي أسلمن مع رسول اللَّه ﵌ بمكّة- جاءت زائرة بني عمها، فقالت: يا آل عامر، ولا عامر لي، يصنع هذا برسول اللَّه ﵌ بين أظهركم ولا يمنعه أحد منكم! فقام ثلاثة من بني عمها إلى بيحرة، فأخذ كلّ رجل منهم رجلا فجلد به الأرض، ثم جلس على صدره، ثم علا وجهه لطما، فقال رسول اللَّه ﵌:
«اللَّهمّ بارك على هؤلاء» . فأسلموا وقتلوا شهداء.
(١) أخرجه أحمد في المسند ١/ ٣٣٠، والدار الدّارقطنيّ ٢/ ٢٣٥، والنسائي في السنن ٥/ ١٦٧ كتاب مناسك الحج باب ٥٩ الاشتراط في الحج حديث رقم ٢٧٦٥- امرؤ القيس حامل لواء الشعر إلى النار ٢/ ١٦٤ أخرجه أحمد في المسند ٢/ ٢٢٨، وابن عساكر ١/ ١١٣، ٣/ ١١١.
(٢) أخرجه البخاري ٧/ ٩ ومسلم في كتاب الحج (١٠٤) .
(٣) أسد الغابة ت (٧٠٧٧)، الاستيعاب ت (٣٤٦٥) .
(٤) في أبيجر.
segments.english:
11430—Duba'a bint Amir

ibn Qurt ibn Salama ibn Qushayr³ ibn Ka'b ibn Rabi'a ibn Amir ibn Sa'sa'a.

Abu Nu'aym mentioned her and transmitted, through Abd Allah ibn al-Ajlah, from al-Kalbi: Abd al-Rahman al-Amiri informed me, from elders of his people, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to us while we were at Ukaz and called upon us to support and protect him. We agreed, but then Bihara⁴ ibn Fihras al-Qushayri came and prodded the flank of the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). It reared with him and threw him off. Duba'a bint Amir ibn Qurt was with us that day. She was among the women who had embraced Islam with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in Mecca, and she had come to visit her paternal cousins. She said: “O Banu Amir—and may I have no kin among Amir!—is this being done to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in your very midst, with not one of you preventing it?” Three of her paternal cousins rose against Bihara. Each one of them seized a man and dashed him to the ground, then sat upon his chest and assailed his face with slaps. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) then said: “O Allah, bless these men.” They embraced Islam and were slain as martyrs.

¹ Recorded in Musnad Ahmad, 1/330; and al-dar [sic] al-Daraqutni, 2/235; and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan, 5/167, Book of the Rites of Pilgrimage, chapter 59, “Stipulating a Condition in the Pilgrimage,” hadith no. 2765—Imru al-Qays, bearer of the banner of poetry to the Fire, 2/164; recorded in Musnad Ahmad, 2/228, and by Ibn Asakir, 1/113 and 3/111.

² Recorded by al-Bukhari, 7/9, and Muslim in the Book of Pilgrimage (104).

³ Usd al-Ghaba, entry 7077; al-Isti'ab, entry 3465.

⁴ Manuscript A reads “Bijar” (vocalization uncertain).

segments.arabic:
وهذا مع انقطاعه ضعيف، وقد وجدت لضباعة هذه خبرا آخر، ذكره هشام بن الكلبي في الأنساب عن أبيه، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عبّاس، قال: كانت ضباعة القشيرية تحت هوذة بن علي الحنفي فمات فورثته من ماله، فخطبها ابن عم لها وخطبها عبد اللَّه بن جدعان، فرغب أبوها في المال فزوّجها من ابن جدعان، ولما حملت إليه تبعها ابن عمها فقال: يا ضباعة، الرجال البخر أحبّ إليك أم الرّجال الذين يطعنون السّور؟ قالت: لا. بل الرّجال الذين يطعنون السّور.
فقدمت على عبد اللَّه بن جدعان، فأقامت عنده، ورغب فيها هشام بن المغيرة، وكان من رجال قريش، فقال لضباعة: أرضيت لجمالك وهيئتك بهذا الشّيخ اللئيم، سليه الطّلاق حتى أتزوّجك، فسألت ابن جدعان الطلاق- فقال: بلغني أنّ هشاما قد رغب فيك، ولست مطلقا حتى تحلفي لي أنك إن تزوجت أن تنحري مائة ناقة سود الحدق بين إساف ونائلة، وأن تغزلي خيطا يمدّ بين أخشبي مكّة، وأن تطوفي بالبيت عريانة.
فقالت: دعني انظر في أمري، فتركها، فأتاها هشام فأخبرته، فقال: أمّا نحر مائة ناقة فهو أهون علي من ناقة أنحرها عنك. وأما الغزل فأنا آمر نساء بني المغيرة يغزلن لك، وأما طوافك بالبيت عريانة فأنا أسأل قريشا أن يخلو لك البيت ساعة، فسليه الطّلاق، فسألته فطلّقها وحلفت له.
فتزوّجها هشام، فولدت له سلمة، فكان من خيار المسلمين، ووفى لها هشام بما قال. قال ابن عبّاس: فأخبرني المطّلب بن أبي وداعة السهمي، وكان لدة رسول اللَّه ﵌، قال: لما أخلت قريش لضباعة البيت خرجت أنا ومحمد ونحن غلامان، فاستصغرونا فلم نمنع، فنظرنا إليها لما جاءت، فجعلت تخلع ثوبا ثوبا، وهي تقول:
اليوم يبدو بعضه أو كلّه ... فما بدا منه فلا أحلّه
[الرجز] حتى نزعت ثيابها، ثم نشرت شعرها فغطّى بطنها، وظهرها حتى صار في خلخالها، فما استبان من جسدها شيء، وأقبلت تطوف، وهي تقول هذا الشعر.
فلما مات هشام بن المغيرة، وأسلمت هي وهاجرت خطبها النبيّ ﵌ إلى ابنها سلمة، فقال: يا رسول اللَّه، ما عنك مدفع، فأستأمرها؟ قال: «نعم» .
فأتاها، فقالت: إنا للَّه! أفي رسول اللَّه تستأمرني؟ أنا أسعى لأن أحشر في أزواجه، ارجع إليه فقل له: نعم قبل أن يبدو له، فرجع سلمة فقال له، فسكت النبيّ ﵌
segments.english:
This report, in addition to having a disconnected chain, is weak. I have found another account concerning this Duba'a, mentioned by Hisham ibn al-Kalbi in al-Ansab, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Duba'a al-Qushayriyya was the wife of Hawdha ibn Ali al-Hanafi. He died, and she inherited some of his wealth. A paternal cousin of hers sought her hand, and Abdullah ibn Jud'an also sought her hand. Her father desired the wealth and therefore married her to Ibn Jud'an. When she was conveyed to him, her cousin followed her and said, “Duba'a, are foul-breathed men dearer to you, or men who pierce ramparts?” She replied, “No—rather, the men who pierce ramparts.”

She came to Abdullah ibn Jud'an and remained with him. Hisham ibn al-Mughira, who was one of the men of Quraysh, desired her. He said to Duba'a, “Are you content that your beauty and fine appearance should belong to this base old man? Ask him for a divorce so that I may marry you.” She asked Ibn Jud'an for a divorce, and he said, “I have heard that Hisham desires you. I will not divorce you until you swear to me that, if you marry, you will slaughter one hundred black-pupiled she-camels between Isaf and Na'ila, spin a thread stretching between the two Akhshabs of Mecca, and circumambulate the Ka'ba naked.”

She said, “Let me consider my affair,” and he left her. Hisham came to her, and she told him. He said, “As for slaughtering one hundred she-camels on your behalf, that is no harder for me than slaughtering one. As for the spinning, I shall order the women of Banu al-Mughira to spin for you. As for your circumambulating the Ka'ba naked, I shall ask Quraysh to clear the Ka'ba for you for a while. So ask him for a divorce.” She asked him, and he divorced her, and she swore the oath to him.

Hisham married her, and she bore him Salama, who became one of the finest Muslims. Hisham fulfilled for her what he had promised. Ibn Abbas said: Al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a al-Sahmi, who was the same age as the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—informed me, saying: “When Quraysh cleared the Ka'ba for Duba'a, Muhammad and I went out, while we were still boys. They considered us too young and did not prevent us. We watched her when she came. She began taking off one garment after another, saying:

Today part of it, or all of it, will appear … Whatever appears of it, I do not make lawful.

[rajaz]

She continued until she had removed her clothes. She then spread out her hair, and it covered her belly and her back until it reached her anklets, so that nothing of her body was visible. She proceeded to circumambulate, reciting these lines.”

When Hisham ibn al-Mughira died, and she had embraced Islam and emigrated, the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—asked her son Salama for her hand. He said, “O Messenger of Allah, there is no refusing you. Shall I seek her consent?” He replied, “Yes.”

He went to her, and she said, “Indeed we belong to Allah! Do you seek my permission concerning the Messenger of Allah? I am striving to be resurrected among his wives. Go back to him and tell him, ‘Yes,’ before he changes his mind.” Salama returned and told him, and the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—fell silent.

segments.arabic:
ولم يقل شيئا، وكان قد قيل له بعد أن ولّى سلمة: إنّ ضباعة ليست كما عهدت، قد كثرت غضون وجهها، وسقطت أسنانها من فمها.
وذكر ابن سعد بعض هذا في ترجمتها عن هشام بن الكلبيّ، وعنه بهذا السّند: كانت ضباعة من أجمل نساء العرب، وأعظمهنّ خلقة، وكانت إذا جلست أخذت من الأرض شيئا كثيرا، وكانت تغطّي جسدها بشعرها.
segments.english:
and said nothing. He had been told, after Salama had turned away, “Duba'a is not as you knew her: the wrinkles on her face have multiplied, and her teeth have fallen from her mouth.”

Ibn Sa'd mentioned some of this in her biographical notice on the authority of Hisham ibn al-Kalbi, and, through him, with this chain of transmission: Duba'a was one of the most beautiful women of the Arabs and one of the largest in physique. When she sat, she took up a great deal of ground, and she used to cover her body with her hair.

unresolved.explanation: The consonantal spelling does not securely determine whether the name should be vocalized Bihara, Bayhara, or otherwise. Bihara is retained provisionally; the collateral witnesses do not resolve the vowels.
The division في أ: بيجر is highly plausible, but the witnesses do not confirm either the division or the vocalization of بيجر. “Bijar” is provisional.
